$comment: Copy to dstack.config.json at your project root and fill in. Dstack has no project knowledge of its own; everything below is what makes it yours. A stage whose command is unset refuses to run and names the missing key. It never guesses and never silently passes.

owner.name: Devin
owner.$comment: The one human whose yes is required at Plan and at Ship. 'reads' is 'evidence' or 'code' and decides how much explaining each stage owes.

plan.$comment: Changes under skipUnderLines may skip the adversarial plan review. The owner's yes may never be skipped.

build.$comment: The builder runs fast because the plan already did the thinking. The reviewer runs deep. Set reasoning depth per invocation, never by editing a shared config mid-run.

prove.$comment: harness mutates each fix back out and requires the named test to fail for the named reason before restoring it.

autoMerge.$comment: Gate refuses to run if this key is true. Nothing merges on a gate result alone.

gate.$comment: Compare each round's in-scope major count to the previous real round. Infrastructure rounds do not count. Two comparisons with no fall means hand it to the owner, not a third round.

seeIt.$comment: Not applicable when no path in appliesWhenChanged is touched. 'Not applicable' is a state the verifier recognizes; 'skipped' is not.

ship.$comment: The full head sha is mandatory. After a squash merge, ancestry is the wrong containment test; verify content per touched file instead.

watch.$comment: Unset means Watch refuses and says so. Set it to whatever proves the deploy landed and nothing was interrupted mid-flight.

ticket.$comment: The marker is generated only by lookupCommand, never written by hand. It is what lets a merge resolve the ticket and email the customer who reported it.

routing.$comment: Jev decides what a stage costs, this file decides what that means. Questions describe the work and never name a model, so the question set does not go stale when the lineup changes. Read skill/references/routing.md before changing a number here.
routing.$comment_escalate: A reading less certain than this routes one rung UP. Uncertainty costs money, never safety. Set to 0 to turn escalation off, which is not recommended.

weights.$comment: Every reading is normalized to 0 through 1 before it is weighted, so a score and a probability are comparable. Only mechanical is negative: following a pattern that is already in the codebase is the one thing that makes a change cheaper to get right.

surfaceFloors.$comment: A floor only ever raises a tier. There are deliberately no surface ceilings: a docs change that measures as high risk is a misclassification, and capping it would be the silent downgrade this whole process exists to remove.

plan.$comment: Replaces skipUnderLines. A plan review is skipped when the change measures as low blast radius on a surface with no floor, not when someone counted lines. The owner's yes is still never skipped.

typical.$comment: Rough tokens this stage reads and writes. Only used to rank models by estimated cost; a wrong guess changes the ranking, never the tier.

build.$comment: surfaceFloorsApply is false because a surface floor is about how hard a change is scrutinized, and Build is not a scrutiny stage. The builder is capped below the top rung on purpose: if a build needs the top rung, the plan was not finished. Plan and Gate still honor every surface floor.

typical.$comment: Rough tokens this stage reads and writes. Only used to rank models by estimated cost; a wrong guess changes the ranking, never the tier.

gate.$comment: The gate is the one stage allowed to cost whatever it costs. Its floor exists so a cheap measurement can never buy a shallow review.

typical.$comment: Rough tokens this stage reads and writes. Only used to rank models by estimated cost; a wrong guess changes the ranking, never the tier.

gate.$comment_pin: Set to a model id in the catalog to force this stage onto it and skip cost ranking. Null means pick the cheapest model that serves the tier.

see.question: user_visible
see.onUnknown: the router could not say whether a customer would see this, so See it runs
see.$comment: Replaces appliesWhenChanged. The threshold is low on purpose: a one in four chance that a customer sees a difference is enough to spend a browser run. This also catches the case the path glob never could, a server side change that alters what is on screen.

models.$comment: Your catalog, and the only list the router may pick from. Prices are US dollars per million tokens, first party Anthropic API rates as of 2026-06-24. 'serves' is the highest work you trust that model with, and it is your call, not the router's: the router only ever picks the cheapest model you already said could do the job. Check live prices at anthropic.com/pricing before trusting a number here.

codex.$comment: A CLI on a subscription, so it has no per token price. An unpriced model is never chosen on cost; it wins only when you pin it or when nothing priced serves the tier.

routing.$comment_provider: Reached through the Vercel AI Gateway, which is a different wire format from TypeSafe direct: a boolean where TypeSafe says noul, and confidence on providerMetadata rather than on the answer. jev.cjs normalizes both. Set provider to typesafe with TYPESAFE_API_KEY to go direct instead.

triage.$comment: Reading the review, not the code. See skill/references/triage.md. The invariant: a reading may only add work or add caution. Set enabled to false and every judgement returns its input unchanged.

infra.$comment: Low on purpose. An unsure reading resolves to infra, which costs one retry, and S4 caps the retry at one and then holds.

findings.$comment: Labels and orders. A cap pads rather than shortens, so a finding past it arrives unread carrying the reviewer's own severity, and the unread count is printed.

plan.$comment: Returns not_ready or no_objection. There is no verdict that means approved.

Set provider to typesafe with TYPESAFE_API_KEY to go direct instead.
